beats.text: Why is this query so slow?
beats.say: Why is this query so slow, on a table with ten million rows?

beats.text: No index: a full table scan, row by row.
beats.say: Without an index, the database does a full table scan. It reads every row, one by one, until it finds a match.

beats.text: An index is a sorted lookup tree (B-tree).
beats.say: An index is a sorted lookup structure, like the index at the back of a book. Most databases use a B-tree.

beats.text: A few hops: root, branch, leaf.
beats.say: Now a lookup takes just a few hops: root, branch, leaf. Even with millions of rows, that's only a handful of steps.

beats.text: But indexes cost space and slow down writes.
beats.say: But indexes aren't free. They take extra space, and every insert or update has to change the index too, so writes get slower.

beats.text: Index what you filter and join on.
beats.say: So index the columns you filter and join on, and skip the rest.
